This example uses a CAM-B3LYP/def2-TZVPP TD-DFT job from `files/` on a chiral organoboron compound
(C26H19BBrN). The job has 50 singlet roots, 50 triplet roots and spin-orbit coupling. A second, very
small job (water, 10 roots, with MO coefficients) shows the charge-transfer analysis.

**Files used** (from the repository):

* `files/1_p8_orca.out` — ORCA, CAM-B3LYP D4 def2-TZVPP CPCM(hexane), `%tddft nroots 50 TDA false dosoc true end`, PrintMOs PrintBasis
* `files/tddft_mos.out` — ORCA, B3LYP def2-TZVPP, `%tddft NRoots 10 end`, PrintMOs PrintBasis, H2O

**1. Excited states, UV-Vis and ECD spectra.** The window is set to 3–6.5 eV (190–413 nm), which covers
the singlets shown in the table. The bands are a bit narrower than the default (`--fwhm 0.25`). Only
transitions with weight above 0.3 are listed. The table has 100 rows (50 S + 50 T), so only the first
ones are shown here.

```bash
frog-tddft files/1_p8_orca.out -t 0.3 --uv --ecd --fwhm 0.25 --x-start 3 --x-end 6.5 --dpi 150 --out-dir spectra
```


```{figure} /_static/cli/frog-tddft/1_p8_orca_ECD.png
:width: 70%
:alt: ECD spectrum (normalised, bands weighted by E·R).

ECD spectrum (normalised, bands weighted by E·R).
```

* S1 (3.669 eV ≈ 338 nm, f 0.477, `H->L (0.82)`) is the lowest band of the UV spectrum. S2
  (4.100 eV, f 0.181) gives the weaker band near 300 nm. The strongest absorptions lie further up in
  energy, where many bright states overlap.
* In the ECD the low-energy states are almost silent (R ≈ 1). The first strong couplet comes from S8
  (R +177.931) and S9 (R −161.150), only 0.03 eV apart: the two signed bands partly cancel. To assign an
  absolute configuration, compare this +/− pattern with the experimental spectrum, after a `--shift`
  if needed.
* S7 and S8 have an empty *Population* column: no single excitation has a weight above `-t 0.3`. These
  states are mixtures; lower `-t` to see their components.

**2. Spin-orbit couplings between selected states.** The full SOC matrix of this job is 51 × 50. With
`--soc-states` only S0, S1 and T1–T4 are kept. Only the SOC table, at the end of the output, is shown.

```bash
frog-tddft files/1_p8_orca.out --soc-states S0 S1 T1-T4
```

```text
…
    Spin-Orbit Coupling (SOC) Matrix
          (files/1_p8_orca.out)
╭───────┬───────┬───────┬───────┬───────╮
│ State │    T1 │    T2 │    T3 │    T4 │
├───────┼───────┼───────┼───────┼───────┤
│ S0    │ 1.285 │ 1.486 │ 3.751 │ 5.329 │
│ S1    │ 0.960 │ 0.414 │ 1.251 │ 1.395 │
╰───────┴───────┴───────┴───────┴───────╯
```

The couplings are a few cm⁻¹: 0.414–1.395 cm⁻¹ between S1 and T1–T4, and up to 5.329 cm⁻¹ between the
ground state and T4. The Br atom is present, but these values are still in the range typical of organic
molecules.

**3. Charge-transfer distance (D_CT) of the first three states of water** on a 40 × 40 × 40 grid, with
a ChimeraX script for the centroids. The excited-state table printed first is omitted here.

```bash
frog-tddft files/tddft_mos.out --dct --dct-states S1-S3 --voxels 40 --chimerax --out-dir dct
```

`dct/tddft_mos_dct.cxc`:

```text
# Δρ centroids of tddft_mos.out (blue: +, red: −)
# S1
shape sphere center -0.002,0.499,-0.000 radius 0.500 color blue
shape sphere center 0.001,-0.365,-0.000 radius 0.500 color red
# S2
shape sphere center -0.001,0.533,-0.000 radius 0.500 color blue
shape sphere center 0.001,-0.354,-0.000 radius 0.500 color red
# S3
shape sphere center -0.001,0.493,-0.000 radius 0.500 color blue
shape sphere center 0.001,-0.558,-0.000 radius 0.500 color red
```

All three states are *Local Exc.*: Δr is 0.86, 0.89 and 1.05 Å, all below the 1.5 Å threshold. The
centroids in the `.cxc` file show that the electron goes from the O side (red, negative Δρ, y between −0.354 and
−0.558 Å) towards the H atoms (blue, y between 0.493 and 0.533 Å). Load the molecule in ChimeraX and `open dct/tddft_mos_dct.cxc`
to draw the two spheres. The three `*_delta_rho.cube` files can be drawn at ±0.002 e/bohr³ or combined
with `frog-cube`.
